text:
leo: Heads up — spotted another friction point in the Go sample app: cancelling generator streams doesn't always stop background auth retries. process goroutines pile up after repeated cancel/restart cycles.
anya: ugh, saw that too on macbook. can repro with sampleapp run-local + repeated Ctrl-C / restart.
pranav: is this the same leak where the refresher uses a global done chan? last time we fixed something similar for non-streaming clients.
leo: similar but not identical. generator creates per-stream conn, refresher is attached to conn and listens on conn.done. on ctx cancel we close the per-request ctx but conn sometimes stays in transient retry state so refresher keeps looping.
tess: can you paste a short stack dump? helps triage.
leo: pasted minimal stack below, gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/go-gen-leak-2145
```
runtime.stack:
1 @ 0x... net/http.(*persistConn).readLoop
1 @ 0x... github.com/redwoodinc/go-sdk/gen.(*streamConn).recvLoop
1 @ 0x... github.com/redwoodinc/go-sdk/auth.(*refresher).run
1 @ 0x... internal/goroutine
```
pranav: looks like refresher.run is blocked in a select waiting on an internal retry timer AND a conn-level channel that isn't closed when request ctx cancels.
anya: two things we should consider: (A) make refresher observe request ctx/deadline; (B) make generator return an explicit stream handle with Close/Err so users don't rely on GC to clean up.
leo: +1 on the API surface. current README example just shows `client.Generate(ctx, ...)` and reads until ctx done, which makes users assume cancel is sufficient.
tess: ergonomics proposal: New API `stream, err := client.Generator(ctx, opts); defer stream.Close()` with methods `(Recv() (Chunk, error), Done() <-chan struct{}, Err() error)`. then stream.Close() cancels underlying conn and stop refresher.
pranav: that also lets us document defers as idiomatic usage. most Go libs expose closeables.
anya: about auth retry semantics: should retries be per-request or per-connection? if per-connection we can keep refresh state across reconnects, but per-request makes cancellation easier.
leo: leaning per-connection for throughput, but refresher must accept a ctx to cancel when the connection is no longer used. connection lifecycle != request lifecycle right now and that's the root cause.
tess: small patch idea: change refresher.run(ctx context.Context, ...) and create a ctx bound to connection that gets canceled on connection.Close() *and* allow caller to pass a per-request ctx to stop it sooner on stream cancel.
pranav: pseudo:
```
func (c *conn) startRefresher(parentCtx context.Context) context.CancelFunc {
  ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parentCtx)
  go func() {
    defer cancel()
    for {
      select {
      case <-ctx.Done():
        return
      case <-time.After(backoff):
        _ = refreshToken()
      }
    }
  }()
  return cancel
}
```
anya: also add unit test: spawn many short-lived streams, cancel immediately, assert goroutine count doesn't grow after GC/polling; and an integration test that simulates 401 from auth and ensures refresher exits on cancel.
leo: I'll file GH issue + link to repro gist and tag eng-runtime + devex.
tess: doc change too — update sampleapp README to show defer stream.Close() and call out that ctx cancel alone may not close connection until internal retry/backoff completes unless you Close().
devops-bot: checklist: add unit test, add integration test, update sampleapp README, RFC API change for returning stream handle, include migration note in changelog.
pranav: who wants to pick the API/impl? I can start a branch for the refresher ctx change.
anya: I can do the sampleapp/README edits and the unit tests.
leo: will own the issue + link PRs. thanks all. :rocket:
tess: small follow-up: consider exposing a `WithImmediateCloseOnCancel` opt for users who want connection destroyed on ctx cancel vs kept for ephemeral retries.
leo: good idea — make it an option to avoid changing defaults mid-release.
anya: ok assigning labels: devex, go-sdk, needs-design.
leo: ping @eng-runtime for design review when PR is ready.
pranav: starting work this afternoon. I'll drop a short design comment on the issue.
